summary: Council approved a package of Community Safety Working Group recommendations including authorization to hire one additional RCMP officer (annual cost $225,000), creation of a $50,000 small business security grant, one full-time bike patrol officer, and up to $50,000 for a Salvation Army service agreement. Council adopted the City of Langford Housing Strategy as presented. Multiple bylaws were adopted or given readings, including zoning amendments for properties on Massie Drive and Madrona Place and first/second/third readings for several permissive tax exemption bylaws and omnibus zoning amendments. Council gave first, second and third readings to Bylaw No. 2302 to rezone 3213 and 3217 Happy Valley Road with conditions. An amendment to the Community Safety motion to add a mural program was defeated with four named oppositions.

motions.motion_text: THAT the main motion be amended by adding "bear spray" to section 7.
motions.plain_english_summary: An amendment to add 'bear spray' to section 7 of the main motion.

motions.motion_text: THAT the main motion be amended by adding section 13: 13. Work with the local artists, with local artists and community groups such as the West Shore Arts Council and West Shore Chamber of Commerce, to explore the creation of a mural program using MRDT funding, and that community murals be added in commercial areas, and in areas where reoccurring tagging is identified as an issue.
motions.plain_english_summary: An amendment to add a mural program using MRDT funding.

motions.motion_text: THAT Council approve the following expenditures from the funds allocated in the budget for initiatives arising from the Community Safety Working Groups: Authorize the hiring of one additional RCMP officer at an annual cost of $225,000. Creation of a small business grant program in the amount of $50,000 to be administered by the West Shore Chamber of Commerce for security improvements. Authorize the addition of one full-time equivalent bike patrol officer. Authorize staff to enter into a service agreement with the Salvation Army for up to $50,000 for the purpose of providing space where members of the community can connect with social services and other supports to mitigate and prevent homelessness. AND THAT Council direct staff as follows: [multiple directions to staff as recorded in the minutes] AND THAT Council further direct staff to send letters to the CRD and the Province advocating for the following: [advocacies as recorded]. AND THAT Council work towards permanent solutions, in conjunction with our West Shore neighbours, to seek a seat at the Region’s Homelessness Encampment Working Group Response Leadership Table advocating to the Province for more varied social housing types, especially transitional housing. AND THAT Council direct staff to bring back a draft Community Safety Plan for consideration before December 31, 2026.
motions.plain_english_summary: Council approved the Community Safety Working Group recommendations and directed staff on multiple follow-up actions.
